items.title: Madra Salach take on “change and betrayal of all kinds” on dark, towering new single ‘Searrach’
items.summary:
Madra Salach have shared their dark, towering new single ‘Searrach’ – check it out below.

READ MORE: Madra Salach live in London: an unmissable live band with incredible power 

The track is the second song to be shared from the rising Dublin six-piece’s debut album ‘Gorta’, after ‘ Ribbon Factory ’, which was released last month.

“We were immediately excited about it after writing and it is one of the moments on the album we’re proudest of,” said singer Paul Banks of the new single. “It is a dark and introspective song about change and betrayal of all kinds, most notably self betrayal. We see it as another stepping stone towards what we’re trying to achieve with the album.”

Their debut is set for release on January 15 via Island Records, and you can pre-order it here . ‘Gorta’ follows the release of their debut EP ‘It’s A Hell Of An Age’.

Produced by Loren Humphrey ( Westside Cowboy , Cameron Winter ) in New York, ‘Gorta’ takes its title from the Irish word for “hunger” and sees the band continue to pay homage to Irish traditional music, but also push their sound into more experimental, darker territories.

The cover was created by Oscar Torrans and captures a Blemmyes – a mythical headless being from medieval lore, whose faces are situated on their chests.

Earlier this year, the Dublin band caught up with NME while at The Great Escape festival , and spoke about how they have seen more and more fans after hitting the live circuit.

“The fact that it’s having this much commercial success is blowing my mind, because my hopes for this project were to find our own little…
items.t: Madra Salach take on “change and betrayal of all kinds” on dark, towering new single ‘Searrach’

items.title: Kieran Culkin defends his “cruel” ‘Sunrise On The Reaping’ character Caesar Flickerman: “I don’t think he intends to be horrible”
items.summary:
Actor Kieran Culkin, known for playing man-baby billionaire scion Roman Roy in TV’s Succession , has teased his latest role in an interview with NME – playing a younger version of The Hunger Games ‘ charismatic TV host Caesar Flickerman. You can watch the filmed interview in full above.

READ MORE: The Hunger Games prequel Sunrise On The Reaping is dividing critics: “An origin story nobody wanted” or a series highlight? 

Stanley Tucci first played Flickerman in the original four blockbuster hit movies starring Jennifer Lawrence , but Culkin has stepped into the presenter’s well-heeled sparkly shoes for new prequel Sunrise On The Reaping . His take on the character has been described as crueller – openly mocking the poor tributes who are competing in the annual televised ‘battle royale’ Hunger Games and seemingly revelling in their misfortune. During one scene, upon meeting the film’s teenage heroes (including Joseph Zada’s central Haymitch Abernathy), he says: “Look alive children… while you still can.”

Culkin doesn’t see Flickerman as irretrievably wicked though. “I think it’s funny that people see it as being cruel,” he said. “It makes sense, but I don’t think he actually intends to be horrible to these people… It’s not a complete lack of empathy.” As the on-screen face of the Hunger Games, Flickerman interviews the contestants on-stage and guides the public through each bloody round via live feed.

Kieran Culkin in ‘The Hunger Games: Sunrise On The Reaping’. CREDIT: Lionsgate UK 
 “He just has to disconnect in order to get through his job,” added Culkin. “His job is…
items.t: Kieran Culkin defends his “cruel” ‘Sunrise On The Reaping’ character Caesar Flickerman: “I don’t think he intends to be horrible”

items.title: Steve Aoki tries to “get a real job” on LinkedIn, gives up two hours later, becomes “thought leader”
items.summary:
Steve Aoki has jokingly posted about his job searching escapades on LinkedIn.

READ MORE: Steve Aoki and Paris Hilton tell us about new collab ‘Lighter’ – and cake-throwing 

The DJ initially set up a profile on the networking site earlier this week declaring that he had decided to “get a real job” on LinkedIn in his first post and “I’m running out of ways to explain to my son why he can’t throw food, but I get paid to do it every night.”

In a second post , with Aoki pictured in a suit, he declared: “Two gruelling hours of job hunting, I’ve made the difficult decision to take an intentional micro-sabbatical.

“I found a remote job that requires three days in the office, wrote a cover letter for a company I discovered 11 minutes ago, and had an existential crisis when asked where I see myself in five years. I don’t even know what time zone I’m in. So I’m stepping back to recharge and focus on what keeps me grounded: traveling the world, DJing until 3AM, and being screamed at by thousands of strangers.”

He added: “I expect to resume my job search later this week. Please respect my privacy during this difficult time.”

Then in a third post , he went on to say he was “back from my sabbatical” and he had “decided to become a thought leader”.

Aoki then mockingly listed what he believes would help his chances of becoming a thought leader including a notes app which is useful for “song ideas, business plans, and a reminder to BUY DIAPERS” a group chat with “792 unread messages. I thumbs-up the latest one so everyone thinks I’m caught up. That’s leadership” and cake which is…
items.t: Steve Aoki tries to “get a real job” on LinkedIn, gives up two hours later, becomes “thought leader”

items.title: The week’s best new tracks and the act you need to know: the rangy folk-prog songwriting of Threshold
items.summary:
Isaac Eiger’s solo venture leaves jangle pop behind for a wilder sound. Often it owes a debt to Alex G, but what indie-rock song doesn’t these days?

From New York via Montana
Recommended if you like Cameron Winter, Tobias Jesso Jr, Alex G
Up next Supporting Caroline on tour in Canada and the US until 19 November

Isaac Eiger is something of a scene legend in the world of American indie-rock. Raised in Bozeman, Montana, he was the founder and lead singer of the cult shoegaze-adjacent six-piece Strange Ranger, who left heartbroken a small, fervent fanbase when they announced their breakup in 2023. Taking a discernibly British approach to their sound, Strange Ranger traversed C86-y jangle-pop before landing on Madchester rave-up for their final album, 2023’s Pure Music. But Eiger is nothing if not musically worldly: he has written and produced with both underground heroes (Cassandra Jenkins, Chanel Beads) and nascent pop stars (Adéla, Frost Children).

Ever-prolific, Eiger also has a solo project under the name Threshold, with which he released a gauzy, 19-minute EP in 2024 called Thief. Earlier this year, he released Stillwater, the first single from the debut Threshold album, due for release in 2027 on the London-based label Untitled. Although Stillwater has some clear influences – it owes some phrasings and intonations to Alex G, but what indie-rock song doesn’t these days? – it’s still a remarkable song: expansive and…
items.t: The week’s best new tracks and the act you need to know: the rangy folk-prog songwriting of Threshold

items.title: Robbie Williams showed up at Jay-Z and Beyoncé’s house, and got turned away
items.summary:
Robbie Williams has recalled how he once turned up at Jay-Z and Beyoncé ‘s house and got turned away.

READ MORE: Robbie Williams plays ‘Britpop’ and debut album in full at tiny London gig: “These songs have reached their destination” 

The pop star explained the incident in a lengthy post on Instagram. Beginning his post, he explained how he made a new friend called “Jay” last summer who invited Williams over to his house.

“For those that don’t know, it takes quite a lot for me to leave my house. Going to somebody else’s house is an even bigger undertaking. It’s not something I do very often,” he said.

Despite that Williams went on to say that he decided to make the journey to his friend’s house but as they got closer the “houses get bigger” and the house numbers “disappeared entirely” which made him begin to feel “anxious”.

View this post on Instagram 

When he found what he thought was his friend’s house, Williams told his driver: “Stop here, mate. This is it.”

“After a moment, a security guard appears with a walkie-talkie. He has the unmistakable demeanour of a man who wasn’t expecting anyone,” he went on. “‘Can I help you?’ ‘Robbie’, I shout cheerfully from the back seat, window down. ‘Here to see Jay.'”

After speaking into his walkie talkie, the security guard asks: “‘Robbie who?'” to which the star replies: “Williams” with “considerably less confidence”.

As the confusion continues Williams then says: “I notice a woman emerging onto the veranda of the enormous house in the distance. I recognise her immediately. It’s Beyoncé’s mum.

“And in a horrible,…
items.t: Robbie Williams showed up at Jay-Z and Beyoncé’s house, and got turned away

items.title: The Biggest Snubs and Surprises at the 2026 ARIA Awards
items.summary:
The 2026 ARIA Awards are in the books , the empties have been discarded and the hangovers (mostly) settled. With the benefit of hindsight, the Australian recording industry’s 40 th annual ceremony at Sydney’s Hordern Pavilion on Wednesday (Nov. 20) was an appropriately large, and noisy, night for such an occasion.

Not for the first time, Kevin Parker was anointed the Australian music community’s boss. And Ecca Vandal deservedly emerged as a hero. For every hero, a villain. Step on up, Artificial Intelligence, the two dirty words on almost every artist’s lips. And for several talents, the night was a real bummer.

Kevin Parker’s psychedelic pop outfit was the big winner, his haul including album of the year for Tame Impala’s fifth studio album, Deadbeat ; best solo artist and song of the year for “Dracula.” Tame Impala also won the second annual Global Impact Award presented by Spotify, a category that launched in 2025 and is designed to sit alongside the ARIA Hall of Fame.

This year’s ARIAs didn’t induct any legends into the ARIA Hall of Fame. That was done in June , when six acts entered the special club with a standalone Hall of Fame presentation. One of those inductees, the beloved rock trio Spiderbait, had the honors of closing the 2026 ARIA Awards with a medley of “Calypso,” “Buy Me A Pony” and “Black Betty.”

The broadcast opened with a proper surprise — Darren Hayes performing Savage Garden’s “Affirmation,” the title track from the world-conquering Brisbane pop duo’s second and final studio album. With the Olympic Games coming to the Sunshine State in 2032, surely…
items.t: The Biggest Snubs and Surprises at the 2026 ARIA Awards

items.title: Muse’s Matt Bellamy wants an AI guitar – but still calls for human-made art and live performance
items.summary:
Muse ‘s Matt Bellamy has admitted that he would like his very own AI guitar.

The band, who are constantly embracing futuristic technology, brought ‘ The Wow! Signal ‘ to The O2 in London for two nights earlier this week and with it an AI robot manning a sound desk adjusting controls as well as singing vocals on a reimagined version of ‘Kill Or Be Killed’, ‘JFK’ and delivering the now iconic drill sergeant speech intro to ‘Psycho’.

Speaking in a new interview with Guitar.com , Muse’s frontman spoke about the prospect of an AI guitar.

“I like the idea of trying to integrate AI components into guitars, where you can prompt a guitar to sound a certain way… I’d like to explore that,” he said. “I like the idea of trying to integrate some of that into guitar, so you can essentially talk to your guitar and tell it how you want it to sound. I’m not quite sure the tech’s there yet, but we’ll see!”

Muse, 2026. Photo credit: Tim Saccenti

“I like the idea of prompting something, but then something analogue happens – that’s interesting to me. I think that’s probably a long way to go before we get that into a guitar, but the idea of it is interesting.”

items.title: ‘GTA 6’ makes more money in one day than ‘The Odyssey’ has in its entire box office run
items.summary:
Grand Theft Auto 6 launched yesterday (November 19) and, according to reports, sold more than 24million copies in its first 24 hours.

READ MORE: ‘Grand Theft Auto 6’ review: one of the best games ever made 

The long-awaited follow-up to 2013’s Grand Theft Auto 5 is reportedly the most expensive video game ever made (it’s budget was rumoured to be more than $1billion) and prior to release, broke pre-order records on both PlayStation and Xbox consoles. It’s also the best-reviewed game of 2026 on review aggregate site Metacritic , and has tied the original The Legend Of Zelda: Ocarina Of Time ’s record as the best-reviewed game of all time with a near-perfect score of 99 per cent.

It’s not just critics who are loving the game either. Fans have taken to social media to praise the massive open-world of Grand Theft Auto 6 and its stacked, bumper soundtrack.

According to analytics company Sensor Tower (via The BBC ), Grand Theft Auto 6 sold more than 24.5million units in its first 24 hours, earning publishers Take Two Interactive $2.36billion in sales. That’s more than The Odyssey ’s entire box office run (which grossed $1.8billion, making it the highest-grossing r-rated film of all time) and comes close to besting 2026’s highest-grossing movie Spider-Man: Brand New Day (which has taken $2.5billion so far).

Rockstar Games and Take-Two Interactive haven’t commented on Grand Theft Auto 6 ’s day one numbers, but the title is expected to top $3billion in sales by the end of 2026. That would make it the highest-grossing video game of all time, but would fall short of the money…
items.t: ‘GTA 6’ makes more money in one day than ‘The Odyssey’ has in its entire box office run

The 12th studio album is the first from Blondie in nine years, following on from 2017’s ‘ Pollinator ’, and was first previewed last month with the lively single ‘ Spectral Eyes ’, featuring Johnny Marr and Glen Matlock .

Now, the New York icons have dropped a second taster of the record in the form of the dynamic ‘Come Back Home’, which sees them join forces with Jess Wolfe and Holly Laessig of Lucius .

Written by the duo and passed on to Blondie for the finishing touches, the song embraces initially ambient and understated melodies, before launching into a powerful, soaring chorus elevated by the unmistakable vocals of Debbie Harry .

“They just gave us a song, and it quickly became one of my favourite things,” guitarist and co-founder Chris Stein told NME . “It’s just fantastic. It reminds me of so much stuff I love and it feels a little country. It’s terrific. I loved it since we heard the demo.”

“We didn’t really work together on it. I just heard the track and thought it was really good for Debbie. It seemed like a perfect fit,” he added, explaining how the collaboration arose. “It all came through John Congleton, our producer. He worked with those guys and passed it along to us. I wasn’t familiar with them before that, but I know they are very renowned in Los Angeles.”…

items.title: The month’s best experimental album: Stella Z’s ambient adventures into lucid dreaming
items.summary:
(CDR)
Based around sounds recorded on her trips back to China, the Fujian-born, London-based producer creates a curious nocturnal collage on Thunder Is the Sky Dreaming

Lucid dreaming is one of the influences behind Thunder Is the Sky Dreaming, the new record from Fujian-born, London-based producer Stella Z. “Every night is an adventure,” she writes in the liner notes, “I can even smell things in certain dreams.” The eight tracks here are suitably sensory, scattered with effervescent sounds, ephemeral whispers and polyrhythmic percussion.

Many of the sounds and textures were recorded during trips back to China – the ambient noises of a pharmacy or the Fujian mountains late at night – a curious, collage-like approach that underpins the record. On The Somnium Is Awaiting My Cue, we hear what appear to be insects buzzing around a plodding bassline and sporadic woodwind motifs, while electronics softly spiral. Similarly hypnotic is Mira Miruna, on which the echoes of words gradually reveal themselves among the fizzing, softly discordant arrangement: a warped, increasingly urgent call to “wake up”, reminiscent of the foggy state as you rise from sleep. Z amplifies this heady feeling later on in Exit, Elsewhere, where her overlapping narration and rattling bells cause total disorientation.

items.t: The month’s best experimental album: Stella Z’s ambient adventures into lucid dreaming

items.title: Jordan Brunoli, Bassist With Australian Indie Rockers Bugs, Dies at 31
items.summary:
Jordan Brunoli, bass player with Brisbane-based indie rock trio Bugs, died on Wednesday night (Nov. 18) following a public battle with cancer. He was 31.

Brunoli was diagnosed with stage 4 colorectal cancer in 2025, and, rather than choosing the quiet life, advocated for others suffering with illness.

The rocker performed on the band’s four albums, including their latest collection, Head Noise , which dropped Aug. 28 and was shortlisted for a J Award for Australian album of the year . The band’s previous album, 2022’s Cooties (via Community Music), crashed the top 10 of the ARIA Top 20 Vinyl Albums Chart, peaking at No. 4.

In 2020, Brunoli and his bandmates had an unexpected breakthrough with their Like A Version cover of Mallrat’s “Charlie,” which broke into the Hottest 100 the following year at No. 91, and landed at No. 25 in 2023’s Hottest 100 Like A Versions of all time poll.

Bugs presented a fundraiser for Brunoli at local venue The Tivoli last October. A slew of Brisbane’s brightest participated in the show, bearing the name Saving A Bug’s Life , including Dear Seattle, Beddy Rays, Sly Withers, Hope D, The Buoys, TOWNS, RAAVE TAPES, and others. 

Following his diagnosis, Jordan was a regular on triple j’s Hack program, on which he shared updates on his health, his outlook as a young person facing a terminal diagnosis, and to remind other young Australians to look after their health.

View this post on Instagram 

He described music as “therapy,” and nothing was better than playing with his bandmates Connor Brooker and Brock Weston.

“Especially when I’m really…
items.t: Jordan Brunoli, Bassist With Australian Indie Rockers Bugs, Dies at 31

items.title: Take That: Dreamers review – 50-something boyband fail to relight the fire on nostalgia-drenched return
items.summary:
(EMI)
The pallid disco revivalism sounds like S Club 7 and the folksy stomp-clap like Mumford and Sons – yet a few standout moments prove they can still strike gold if they try

Listening to Wonderkids, the string-laden opener of Take That’s new album, it seems the three remaining fiftysomething boybanders are feeling reflective. “Forgiving you, forgiving me / This vicious circle is now complete,” sings Gary Barlow.

In the years since their last record, the band – and former member Robbie Williams – have indeed laid out the trials and tribulations of 35 years of Take That in several documentaries, some more candid than others. Earlier this year, they even embarked on a revival of their blockbuster 2009 Circus tour. Unfortunately, all this reminiscing has left their 10th album feeling so steeped in nostalgia that any moments of greatness struggle for attention.

items.title: U2 Ride to No. 1 on ARIA Chart With ‘Carnaval De Luz’
items.summary:
U2 ’s Carnaval De Luz (via Island/Universal) enjoys the brightest possible start on the Australia’s albums chart , as it opens at No. 1.

With that fast opening, Carnaval De Luz becomes the Irish rock legends’ 12th chart leader in these parts. The Rock And Roll Hall of Fame inductees bagged their first No. 1 album with The Unforgettable Fire in 1984, a year after the ARIA Charts launched, and kept the hits coming with Rattle and Hum (1988), Achtung Baby (1991), Zooropa (1993), Pop (1997), The Best Of 1980-1990 (1998), All That You Can’t Leave Behind (2000), The Best Of 1990-2000 (2002), How To Dismantle An Atomic Bomb (2004), U218 Singles (2006), and No Line On The Horizon (2009).

According to ARIA, U2’s dozen No. 1s places the foursome equal fourth on the all-time leaderboard, tied with Madonna, and behind only The Beatles and Taylor Swift (14 each) and leader Jimmy Barnes with 16. Including Cold Chisel recordings, Barnes has 22 ARIA No. 1s.

The latest ARIA Chart, published Friday, Nov. 20, is something of a birthday party for a bunch of veteran acts. Those celebrating include Aphex Twin , whose 25 th anniversary edition of Drukqs (Warp/Inertia) drops in at No. 14, for the British electronic music great’s highest-charting album, bettering the No. 45 for Selected Ambient Works Volume II .

Also, the late king of pop, Michael Jackson , returns to the chart at No. 21 with his former leader, Invincible , following its 25 th anniversary release. And Australian punk rock act Trophy Eyes bounces in at No. 24 with 10 th anniversary edition of Chemical Miracle .

items.title: Gracie Abrams’ ‘Daughter from Hell’ Gets Deluxe Treatment: Stream It Now
items.summary:
Gracie Abrams ’  Daughter from Hell is now, well, more hell-ish.

The Grammy nominated singer and songwriter today (Nov. 20) drops the deluxe edition of Daughter from Hell , an expanded version that now features five fresh cuts.

Daughter from Hell (Deluxe) collects newbies “Out of Nowhere,” which became a fan fave after Abrams debuted it during her 2025 Glastonbury Festival spot (where Paul McCartney was watching on from the sidelines); and “Crazy Girl,” which appeared on the vinyl exclusive and is now available digitally for the first time. Other bonus tracks into the previously revealed “Here You Come, There You Go,” produced by Jim-E Stack and co-written with Amy Allen; “Love Letter;” and “Lost It In.”

It’s not the first expansion for Daughter From Hell . In late July , Abrams added two additional tracks from the DFH sessions to the standard version: “Out of Nowhere” and “Love Letter”. As it stands, the album blows out to 21 songs, with a playing time of 70 minutes.

The “Daughter From Hell” in the title really is Abrams. “That song was the last one that I wrote for the album, and it is like a, you know, decades overdue apology to my mom, basically,” she told Jimmy Fallon during an episode of NBC’s The Tonight Show , which aired in July. Was she a beastly kid? Not exactly, just a “defiant person,” which can be “turbulent” for mom and dad (the film director J.J. Abrams). “This is a thank-you note to her.”

Abrams scored her first No. 1 album on the Billboard 200 chart with Daughter From Hell , which opened atop the Aug. 1-dated ranking.

items.title: ‘Grand Theft Auto VI’ Soundtrack, Gracie Abrams, LISA, Tomorrow x Together & More: New Music Friday Guide
items.summary:
Billboard’s Friday Music Guide serves as a handy guide to New Music Friday’s most essential releases each week — the key music that everyone will be talking about today, and that will be dominating playlists this weekend and beyond.

Last week , we featured The Hunger Games soundtrack, ATEEZ and U2 Feat. Dolly Parton.

This week, the jam-packed and starry soundtrack for GT6 is out; Gracie Abrams drops the deluxe edition of Daughter From Hell ; and TOMORROW x TOGETHER share a new EP… plus much more.

Check out all of this week’s picks below:

Grand Theft Auto VI: The Album 

The video game that defined a generation is back with a new edition — and a star-studded soundtrack to boot. Featuring contributions from Dua Lipa, Cardi B, Morgan Wallen, Tame Impala, King Gizzard and the Lizard Wizard, SZA, Travis Scott, Justice, JENNIE, Lana Del Rey, Zara Larsson and Rauw Alejandro, Grand Theft Auto VI: The Album translates the game’s high-octane, gun-toting world into music spanning hip-hop, dance, Latin, country and more. Even though 10 tracks were released ahead of the full album, this towering compilation has more than enough new material for both gamers and casual listeners to sink their teeth into. — KYLE DENIS

items.title: ‘We’re the most arrogant of all apes!’ A delightfully mind-expanding encounter with Peter Gabriel
items.summary:
From sampling to streaming, the rock legend has always been in thrall to technology – but is superintelligence a step too far? Back with an epic new album, he unpacks his remarkable ideas

Peter Gabriel asks me to fetch my laptop: he wants to show me a video of himself playing a keyboard duet with a bonobo called Kanzi. In fairness, said footage is, as Gabriel suggests, “extraordinary”. Working with primatologist Sue Savage-Rumbaugh, who developed a means of communicating with bonobos involving sign language and a speech-synthesis keyboard, Gabriel plays droning chords on a synthesiser while Kanzi picks out complementary notes on a piano. “Look, she likes that note, which is a ninth, and then she finds the octave,” he enthuses as the video plays. “There’s a real musicality there.”

It is all deeply unlikely, but it seems the perfect illustration of how easily a conversation with Gabriel can go wildly – if fascinatingly – off-piste. I’ve only been in his company for 10 minutes, long enough to ask a solitary question about his epic new album o\i: its 13 tracks last nearly 90 minutes, the result, he suggests, of a longstanding interest in African music “which made me realise that a song could last as long as a song could last”, and of “being old enough to think ‘fuck it’, really”. For anyone who feels that an hour and a half of exquisitely arranged, beautifully produced, occasionally deeply strange art rock – its sound shapeshifting from the folk-flecked A Hard Lesson to the glowing pop hues of Till Your Mind Is Shining – is too meagre an offering, it arrives in…
items.t: ‘We will become cyborgs!’ Peter Gabriel on bonobo ape duets, building a Jurassic Park for plants – and why AI will make great music

items.title: Childish Gambino’s Politically-Charged ‘This Is America’ Joins YouTube’s Billion Views Club
items.summary:
Childish Gambino has joined the club. YouTube’s Billion Views Club, that is, for his 2018 hit “This Is America.” 

The official music video for the actor and rapper’s global smash is his first to pass the streaming milestone.

“This Is America’ was a politically-charged shot that rung out around the globe, a song that explores gun violence, racism and discrimination in the United States. It was, of course, powered by its confronting, one-take music video , directed by Hiro Murai and starring Gambino.

The recording debuted at No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100 chart (via mcDJ/Wolf + Rothstein/RCA), bowing as the most-streamed and top-selling song of the week. It also arrived atop the U.S. Streaming Songs and Digital Song Sales charts, and topped sales and consumption charts around the globe, including Australia .

The single was the first and only Hot 100 leader for Donald Glover’s musical alter ego, who took the stage to unveil it as the musical guest on the May 5, 2018 episode of NBC’s Saturday Night Live , which he also hosted.

On the red carpet of the 2018 Met Gala, Glover spoke briefly about the song and its meaning. In a comment dripping with irony, he remarked that, with “This Is America,” he simply wanted to make a song folks could play on the Fourth of July.

He elaborated in a 2023 interview for a GQ cover story, in which he said the idea for the song “started as a joke,” and that its title was “all we had” at the embryonic stage. “It started as a Drake diss, to be honest, as like a funny way of doing it. But then I was like, this s— sounds kind of hard though. So I…

items.title: Darren Hayes Launches the 2026 ARIA Awards With Savage Garden’s ‘Affirmation’: Watch
items.summary:
Savage Garden is, sadly, long gone. But when Darren Hayes took the stage at the 2026 ARIA Awards on Wednesday night (Nov. 18) in Sydney, he reminded everyone tuned in exactly what they were missing.

Hayes got the 40 th anniversary ARIAs broadcast underway — and the emotions stirring — with a performance of “Affirmation,” the title track from Savage Garden’s second and final album from 1999.

It was both a surprise for guests, and a proper highlight, its lyrics resonating just as they did on release more than a quarter century ago. 

Hayes wasn’t done there. He returned to the ARIAs stage to present Tame Impala  spearhead Kevin Parker with the ARIA Global Impact Award, in recognition of his extraordinary international success and cultural impact in the past year.

For Hayes and his ex-Savage Garden bandmate Daniel Jones, the ARIA Awards is a warm and fuzzy place. At the 1997 edition, the pop group dominated with a then-record 10 wins, including album of the year and group of the year.

Savage Garden would collect a total of 14 career ARIAs, including the best-selling album award in 2000 for Affirmation , before disbanding in 2001.

The Brisbane group flew the flag high during their active years, and became one of a select handful of Australian groups to enjoy a No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100. Indeed, they did it twice: with 1998’s “Truly Madly Deeply,” and again in 2000 with “I Knew I Loved You,” while their 1997 track “I Want You” also entered the top 5 (peaking at No. 4). Both albums ( Savage Garden at No. 3, Affirmation at No. 6) cracked the top 10 of the Billboard 200.…
items.t: Darren Hayes Launches the 2026 ARIA Awards With Savage Garden’s ‘Affirmation’: Watch

items.title: Is Lorenzo Senni’s All Ages the year’s wildest electronic album?
items.summary:
(Warp)
The Milan producer revisits his youth as a straight-edge punk fan voyeuristically dabbling in rave – and finds a thrilling interzone between both genres

The opening line of the biography on Lorenzo Senni’s Bandcamp page is striking. “Lorenzo Senni was never a raver,” it reads, something of a blunt admission from a dance producer, or at least a producer who works in an area of electronica influenced by dance music: one might reasonably assume you need some first-hand experience of the dancefloor’s ineffable freedom in order to make music for it. But the Milan-based Senni has made a USP out of his arm’s length distance from what that Bandcamp bio calls a “neon-hued chemical world”.

A straight-edge punk fan in the late 90s, he accompanied friends to Rimini’s hardcore and gabber clubs as a kind of anthropological exercise, a self-styled “rave voyeur” who “just liked to observe and analyse my surroundings”. Accordingly, his albums to date have dealt in what approving critics like to call deconstructions or interrogations of dance music rather than dance music itself: 2012’s Quantum Jelly and 2014’s Superimpositions featured what Senni called “pointillistic trance”, spinning the icy, staccato notes and arpeggiated synth lines of the genre’s epic breakdowns into lengthy, beatless tracks that never reached the climax implied. Released at the height of the 2020 Covid lockdown – when everyone was, by default, some distance from the dancefloor – his last album,
items.t: Trance, prog synths, guttural screaming: Lorenzo Senni’s All Ages is the year’s wildest electronic album

items.title: ‘I have to sell my bum on OnlyFans to go on tour’: Kate Nash on fame, feminism and fighting the music business
items.summary:
She threw a (metaphorical) brick through Spotify’s window and exposed industry failings with her ‘Butts for Tour Buses’ campaign. Now the singer is embracing her Irish roots with her new album’s fighting spirit

Kate Nash was standing on a fire truck in a showgirl outfit complete with white tights and pink G-string, shouting through a loudhailer about the music industry’s failure to pay artists fairly, when she wondered if she’d gone too far. It was 2024 and the truck, which made pit stops outside the London offices of Spotify and Live Nation, had a large black-and-white picture of Nash’s bum on the back along with the words “Butts for Tour Buses” – a reference to her newly launched OnlyFans account, which she was using to fund her tour.

That afternoon, she called her manager Kat. “I told her: ‘I’ve thrown a brick through the window at Spotify.’ She went: ‘What, literally?’ and I said: ‘No, but I’ve been standing outside their offices with a megaphone, so that relationship is over. I don’t think we’ll be making their New Music Friday feature.’ And we didn’t.” [see footnote]

items.title: Ocean Colour Scene review – no other band of their era can do it like this
items.summary:
Ulster Hall, Belfast
With two sets of fathers and sons now in the group, as they play all of Moseley Shoals on its 30th anniversary, the indie stalwarts have aged into seismic and soulful performers

‘It’s only 30 years ago,” Simon Fowler says of Moseley Shoals. He would seem to mean it, but 30 years makes Ocean Colour Scene’s breakthrough album as old now as Revolver was when they were making it. The band once derided for raiding the 60s are now heritage themselves. They open the album’s anniversary tour on the stage where Led Zeppelin first played Stairway to Heaven, and you can’t help but appreciate the lineage.

They walk on to Green Onions, fresh from the Crown Bar, and open with You’ve Got It Bad, all supreme Motown stomp. Fowler sings with a hand in his pocket and looks taken aback by the welcome. The casualness is a conduit: his voice has aged into something close to peak Joe Cocker, grained at the edges, honey underneath. Lining Your Pockets is more resounding than ever.
